description: A four-panel composite of EBSD inverse-pole-figure (IPF) orientation colour maps of Nb-containing medium-Mn low-density steels, each panel covering the same field-size with a black scale bar labelled "20μm" in the lower-right corner. (a) is the as-cast 0.02Nb steel: large, elongated interlocking colour domains outlined by black high-angle grain boundaries, with numerous small isolated domains of contrasting colour embedded inside them. (b) is the 0.02Nb steel aged at 823 K for 3 h: the map is much more fragmented, composed of many small equiaxed colour regions plus dark slivers and small islands. (c) is the as-cast 0.04Nb steel: intermediate-size colour domains plus an inset IPF colour triangle with corners labelled 111 (top), 001 (bottom-left) and 101 (bottom-right). (d) is the 0.04Nb steel aged at 823 K for 3 h: large blue, cyan, green and pink domains with many small internal islands. All maps use the same rainbow IPF colour scheme keyed to the crystal direction parallel to the sample normal, and grain boundaries are drawn as thin black lines; no numeric grain-size or orientation values are printed on any panel. The group demonstrates that Nb content and the 823 K/3 h ageing treatment change the austenite/ferrite grain morphology and the amount of intragranular sub-structure.

observations.observation: All four panels are EBSD inverse-pole-figure orientation colour maps with grain boundaries drawn as thin black lines.
Every panel carries a black scale bar labelled '20μm' in the lower-right corner.
Panel (c) contains an inset IPF colour triangle with the three corners labelled 111, 001 and 101, indicating the colour-to-crystal-direction key.
The caption identifies panel (a) as the as-cast 0.02Nb steel and panel (b) as the 0.02Nb steel aged at 823 K for 3 h.
The caption identifies panel (c) as the as-cast 0.04Nb steel and panel (d) as the 0.04Nb steel aged at 823 K for 3 h.
No numeric grain size, orientation angle or phase fraction is printed anywhere in the figure; the only printed number is the 20μm scale bar.

The map in (b) is visibly more fragmented into small equiaxed colour domains than the map in (a), i.e. the aged 0.02Nb condition shows a finer subdivision of orientation domains than the as-cast 0.02Nb condition.
Maps (a), (b) and (d) contain numerous small isolated domains of contrasting colour enclosed within larger grains, whereas (b) shows these features together with dark elongated slivers.
The citing text states that increasing Nb content refines the austenite grain size, as shown in Figure 5.
The citing text attributes the grain refinement to more intergranular NbC particles in the 0.04Nb steels hindering austenite grain-boundary motion.

The paper abstract states that the austenite grain size of 0.04Nb steels is approximately half that of 0.02Nb steels; this quantitative factor is not measurable from the maps, which carry no printed size values.
